title: Daily Stablecoin Policy Brief - 2026-07-31
executiveSummary: U.S. implementation of the GENIUS Act is advancing through OCC and interagency proposals, including OCC rules for issuers under its jurisdiction and customer-identification requirements for permitted payment stablecoin issuers.
The interagency customer-identification proposal is open for comment through 2026-08-22 and would treat permitted payment stablecoin issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act.
The United Kingdom's Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 identifies issuance of qualifying stablecoins as a regulated activity when specified conditions are carried out in the United Kingdom.

topDevelopments.headline: OCC proposal advances GENIUS Act implementation for entities under OCC jurisdiction
topDevelopments.signal: The OCC proposed regulations to implement the GENIUS Act for payment stablecoin issuance and related activities by entities under OCC jurisdiction. The proposal clarifies that permitted payment stablecoin issuers established in U.S. territories are excluded from the definition of foreign payment stablecoin issuers.
topDevelopments.whyItMatters: The proposal provides a direct federal implementation path for OCC-regulated issuers under a framework that limits payment stablecoin issuance to permitted issuers and includes reserve, redemption, disclosure, reserve-reuse, and Bank Secrecy Act requirements.
affectedParties: Stablecoin issuers established in U.S. territories

topDevelopments.headline: Federal agencies propose customer-identification standards for permitted payment stablecoin issuers
topDevelopments.signal: FinCEN, the OCC, the Federal Reserve, the FDIC, and the NCUA proposed a rule requiring permitted payment stablecoin issuers to maintain effective customer identification programs. The proposal is open for comment through 2026-08-22.
topDevelopments.whyItMatters: The proposal would operationalize the GENIUS Act treatment of permitted payment stablecoin issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act, increasing onboarding and compliance-control expectations for issuers.

topDevelopments.headline: UK statute identifies qualifying stablecoin issuance as a regulated activity
topDevelopments.signal: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 identifies issuance of qualifying stablecoins as a regulated activity where specified conditions are carried out in the United Kingdom and addresses jurisdiction for certain regulated cryptoasset activities involving consumer sales or subscriptions.
topDevelopments.whyItMatters: Issuers and firms serving UK-facing consumer activity need to assess whether their stablecoin issuance and related cryptoasset activities fall within the stated regulated-activity and jurisdiction provisions.
affectedParties: Firms offering cryptoassets to UK consumers

regulatorySignalTable.signal: OCC proposed GENIUS Act implementation rules for payment stablecoin issuance by entities under OCC jurisdiction.
regulatorySignalTable.direction: Toward federal operationalization of a permitted-issuer framework.
regulatorySignalTable.businessImpact: OCC-regulated issuers should assess alignment with the GENIUS Act framework, including one-to-one reserves, redemption procedures, monthly reserve disclosures, limits on reserve reuse, and Bank Secrecy Act requirements.

regulatorySignalTable.signal: Interagency customer-identification proposal for permitted payment stablecoin issuers is open for comment through 2026-08-22.
regulatorySignalTable.direction: Toward explicit Bank Secrecy Act customer-identification obligations for permitted issuers.
regulatorySignalTable.businessImpact: Issuers may need to build or enhance customer-identification governance, controls, onboarding processes, and related compliance operations.

regulatorySignalTable.signal: Federal Reserve proposals would create special-purpose Payment Accounts for certain payment activity, potentially including eligible nonbank entities; the accounts would have zero reserve requirements and would not earn interest.
regulatorySignalTable.direction: Toward a potential specialized Federal Reserve account-access category with defined limitations.
regulatorySignalTable.businessImpact: Eligible stablecoin providers and payment firms may monitor potential account-access eligibility, while accounting for the absence of interest and discount-window eligibility under the related proposals.

regulatorySignalTable.signal: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 identifies issuance of qualifying stablecoins as a regulated activity when specified UK conditions are met.
regulatorySignalTable.direction: Toward statutory treatment of qualifying stablecoin issuance within regulated financial-services activity.
regulatorySignalTable.businessImpact: Issuers and platforms should evaluate UK activity, consumer-facing distribution, and related disclosure or advertising exposure under the applicable cryptoasset framework.

regulatorySignalTable.signal: The Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act would define permitted payment stablecoins by reference to the GENIUS Act and limit CFTC jurisdiction over them; it has been placed on the Senate Legislative Calendar.
regulatorySignalTable.direction: Toward delineating CFTC treatment of permitted payment stablecoins.
regulatorySignalTable.businessImpact: Firms involved in digital commodity transactions involving permitted payment stablecoins should monitor potential jurisdictional and transaction-treatment changes.

marketImpact.stablecoinIssuers: The principal near-term policy impact is heightened federal compliance preparation: OCC implementation rules and the proposed customer-identification requirement reinforce the permitted-issuer, reserve, redemption, disclosure, and Bank Secrecy Act framework. UK qualifying stablecoin issuers also face a regulated-activity signal where specified UK conditions apply.
marketImpact.exchangesAndWallets: Platforms and wallet providers should monitor the UK treatment of regulated cryptoasset activities involving consumer sales or subscriptions, and assess how issuer customer-identification obligations could affect stablecoin onboarding and transaction relationships.
marketImpact.paymentCompanies: The Federal Reserve's proposed special-purpose Payment Accounts may be relevant to certain payment activity and potentially eligible nonbank entities, but the proposals describe zero reserve requirements, no interest on account balances, and no discount-window eligibility.
marketImpact.defiProtocols: The provided materials focus on issuer regulation, payment-account access, and regulated cryptoasset activities rather than protocol-specific requirements. Protocols with exposure to permitted payment stablecoins should monitor issuer compliance changes and potential CFTC jurisdictional delineation.

watchlist: Comments on the permitted payment stablecoin issuer customer-identification proposal close on 2026-08-22.
Further OCC implementation measures for the GENIUS Act, including treatment of issuer licensing, foreign-issuer registration, AML/CFT, sanctions compliance, redemption access, and reporting.
Federal Reserve decisions following closed comments on special-purpose Payment Accounts, Regulation A, and Regulation D proposals.
Progress of the Digital Commodity Intermediaries Act on the Senate Legislative Calendar.
Application of UK qualifying-stablecoin regulated-activity provisions to issuer and consumer-facing cryptoasset activity.
analystTakeaway: The clearest current policy signal is implementation rather than a new statutory framework: U.S. agencies are translating the GENIUS Act into issuer supervision and customer-identification requirements, while the UK statutory framework identifies qualifying stablecoin issuance as regulated activity under specified conditions. Compliance planning should prioritize issuer eligibility, customer identification, reserve and redemption controls, and jurisdiction-specific distribution analysis.
